notes.title: Moonstone Island Demo Out Now!
notes.content:
[b]You there! Game-player![/b]

Have you ever found yourself questioning life? Of course you have! Life is chaos! Life is confusing! Life is something you get handed to you at birth with zero instructions or hints! But what if there were a way to [i]try [/i]something before [i]buying[/i] it, so to speak?

Wonder no more! We at Moonstone Island Labs have invented a new thing we're calling a DEMO, short for "demonstration", which allows you to give something a go in a short, controlled fashion before you make your decision on whether or not you want it!

In this "demo", which we're releasing today, you can trial the fantastic (and currently on sale!) game that is Moonstone Island, COMPLETELY FREE! 

Free, you say? How can such a thing be free?! Well, therein lies the catch, chums: this demo grants you access to the first two weeks of the game, which take place in the springtime. During those two weeks, you will get to experience what it's like to play Moonstone Island, completely [i]gratis![/i] 

And if, at the end of those two weeks, you decide that you want to see more, then GOOD NEWS! You can purchase the game (ON SALE FOR 40% OFF!!!) and your save game will continue into the full game, no restarts needed!

We're really hoping this "demo" thing catches on, and if it does, remember to tell your friends: Moonstone Island invented that thing! We're the first ones to ever do it! Patent pending!

Lots of love,
– Kate, Community Manager and Co-Inventor of Demos

notes.title: Fishbo Fools Update!
notes.content:
[b]Happy April, dear ones! It's Magic Man, or Waldo, perhaps you know me as, yes.[/b]

In the old kingdom, the first of April was a most special day – a day for rejoicing in the strange, the arcane, the unusual – much like me, oho! 

And I indeed have something strange, arcane, and unusual to show you today. In my magical experimentation, I discovered something most peculiar, revealed to me by my darling Fishbo Junior in whispers at night. I am calling them...

FISHBO VARIANTS.

You see, under the right conditions, a Fishbo can transfer its very essence to other Spirits, transforming them into Fishbo-like creatures, while still retaining parts of their own original essence, yes! These new Spirits sprout legs and grow bowls around their bodies, becoming as Fishbo, but still yet something... unique, and special. It is said that any Fishbo that appears in the world will have a small chance of being one of these mutations! How interesting, yes!

I hope you will find some of these rare and wonderful Spirits yourself, and you will say to yourself, "ah, Waldo, what a genius you are, yes!" And then I hope you will bring them to say hello to Fishbo Junior. It was his idea, after all.

Happy April, my dear ones! Ah, no, I already said that. Well, goodbye, then!
– Waldo, AKA Magic Man

notes.title: Anniversary Update Patch Notes
notes.content:

It was our birthday on the 20th, and now it's our big update day, which means it's time for a SPECIAL birthday-themed patch notes! You can just leave all your gifts in the corner over there. Also, take one of these party poppers, and you can set it off at the end: 🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉

Let's start with the new things!

[*] Increased tab size in settings menu for all platforms
[*] Updated “exhaust” icon on cards to look more like a bin, because "bin" is a better indicator of exhaust than a red arrow
[/list]

Now the bug fixes! I made sure they're birthday-cake-flavoured, so open wide:

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] You can't put warp totems (and other special items) in chests anymore

Okay, let's set off the party poppers now. YAY, BIRTHDAY!
🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉

notes.title: Cooking Update - Detailed Patch Notes!
notes.content:
Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to the first episode of Patch Notes Kitchen, with me, Kate – I mean, Moonstonio McChefhat, famous TV cooking guy! 

Today we're making a tasty three-course meal: a Bugfixes Soufflé, followed by a hearty Marinated Content Steak served with Baby New Spirits, and for dessert, DLC! Which stands for Delicious Layer Cake, obviously.

The first step in this recipe is to add the following to your game:

[h2]New Content[/h2]
[list]
[*] The ability to COOK!
[*] New crafting stations (prep table, stove, recipe book)
[*] Dozens of meals with unique effects
[*] New cooking questline (given by Ossono on Spring 16 or a few days after updating for in-progress games)
[*] New LORE
[*] New cooking-themed decorations
[*] Four new spirits: Eleplant (water), Jelbell (psychic), Grampus (ice), and Fangface (dark)
[*] New NPC likes/dislikes (spoiler: they're all meals)
[/list]

Now that the Content Steak is in the oven, prepare your Bugfixes Soufflé! Here are some notes on how to make it:

[h2]Bugfixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Did you use a broom/fishing rod/warp whistle near a shrine or a warpstone, and accidentally activate it instead of using the item? Not any more! We fixed it
[*] Used the correct font for the "purchased" text in other languages
[*] You can no longer feed Spirits old boots. Also, don't do that! Ew!
[*] Increased the size of the white circle shown when activating the Ando tree, because you cool dudes with ultra-wide monitors weren't getting the full effect
[*] Magic Man's house was appearing underneath the swimming pool. He's mysterious and strange, but not THAT mysterious and strange, so we changed that
[*] You can no longer feed Spirits multiple stat reset potions to cause them to gain points somehow. I'm continually impressed by all these cheats but we must fix them, sorry
[*] You can no longer feed fish to Spirits in battles. Apparently Fishbo assumed it was a mean intimidation tactic and he got really upset
[*] Tobin bought some glow-in-the-dark paint online, and now the fishing bobber lights up at night for easier fishing
[*] Restored Magic Man's missing dialogues – he's meant to say stuff after you pick up the temple seals!
[*] You can no longer steal Zed's museum of Spirit resources. CONGRATULATIONS, YOU INVENTED STEALING ON A PEACEFUL ISLAND. You monsters.
[*] You can't place furniture in other people's houses and workplaces any more. I mean, I know Quill's taste in decor is very "guy who owns a single armchair and a PlayStation 5", but he has to learn that on his own, k?
[/list]

And finally, the Delicious Layer Cake, also known as the Chef's Kiss DLC, is live today. It's a paid DLC, but it's decor only! 

As a reminder of what it includes:
[list]
[*] Bakery House Skin
[*] Donut Rug
[*] Cloche
[*] Pot Rack
[*] Marble Counter
[*] Marble Counter with Sink
[/list]

Aaaand that's everything! All of these bugfixes + more will also be coming to the Switch today, as well as the Pool Party DLC and Russian language options, so if you're also playing on the Nintendo RectangleTM, then it should run a lot more smoothly now.

As always, you're the best. Mwah.

notes.title: Magic May Update - Detailed Patch Notes!
notes.content:
[b]It's nearing the end of Magic May, which means we're adding a ton of stuff to the game[/b] – new furniture, new dialogue, new Spirits, and all of that. But we've already talked about that. You know all that. Today, my friends, I have brought you here to talk about the thing we love most (at least I do) – PATCH NOTES.

It's a long one, so we've split it up into four categories: Big Things, Small Things, Magic Man Things, and Bug Things. I mean, fixes. Bug Fixes. Let's start off with our man of the month, Magic Man!

[h2]Magic Man Things[/h2]
[list]
[*] Magic Man discovered a new, forbidden kind of card magic, and as a result he's developed dozens of new "shop exclusive" cards. Don't call the card police pls
[*] He's also finally learned how to actually, you know, leave the house. Once Waldo moves to Moonstone Island, he will now walk around instead of staying inside all the time. He'll even go to the Tavern!
[*] Waldo has more to say once he's moved back, too. There's a lot of new dialogue from both him and the other NPCs that acknowledge his presence instead of awkwardly ignoring him all the time. No wonder he never left the house before.
[*] We've added a few Magic Man-themed decorations to the game! Some are DLC, and some are part of the free update. There's a lot of purple, a lot of magic, and even a few things shaped like Waldo's ✨ iconique ✨ hat
[/list]
That's it for Waldo stuff. Let's move on to the Big Things!

[h2]Big Things[/h2]
[list]
[*] Ten! New! Inventory! Slots!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Can you think of a single game that has ever given you inventory expansions after launch? It's probably never been done. We're pocket pioneers, baby
[*] And while we're at it: You get a second tool wheel! You get a second tool wheel! EVERYBODY GETS A SECOND TOOL WHEEEEEEL
[*] Four! New! Spirits!!! One of them is a shrub with legs, and I love him. Also, Pombomb from Cassette Beasts is in Moonstone Island now! Synergy!!!!!!!
[*] Step into the amazing new world of MAP ZOOMING, where you can see each island much bigger than before! Bonus: It makes matching islands to treasure maps roughly ten billion times easier
[*] Animated house exterior!! ANIMATED HOUSE EXTERIOR!!!!! It's a big ol' fishbowl, because we know you all want to live like Fishbo lives. This one's free for everyone. I mean... it's on the house 😉
[*] Trees now have a chance of dropping saplings when cut down, which is only horrifying if you think about it too much
[*] Furnaces can now smelt multiple ingots because we're all too darn busy to babysit a fire forever
[*] More furnace news: you can now add ore and coal to the furnace while it's running. If you burn yourselves we are not liable ok
[*] We updated the save system! It now automatically organizes games into separate files, so you won't curse the day the developers were born every time you accidentally overwrite a save. Side note: please stop cursing the day we were born
[*] Zed has been building a computer in his spare time... and it was for you! Now you can use it to access Spirit Storage after hours
[*] Does the gigantic empty space of the basement make you nervous? Split that bad boy up into smaller rooms like a greedy landlord with our new placeable walls! They can be rotated, placed anywhere, used to hang decor, and even wallpapered like regular walls!
[*] Tobin's been working hard on Fish ScienceTM, and he's developed a few new fishing lures that will help you catch specific fish to fill out that trophy shelf
[*] XP is now a lot easier to get, because we're not about that grind
[*] NAPPING UNLOCKED. Head to your bed to take a lil snoozy-woozy and refill your energy at any time
[*] Fibre is now purchasable in the workshop
[*] Added Russian language! Ура!
[/list]
Okay, woww. That was so many big things. What's next?

[h2]Small Things[/h2]
[list]
[*] Mass manufacture ENABLED! Craft multiple items at once by pressing and holding the craft button!
[*] Mass feeding ENABLED! Give your Spirits the mukbang they deserve by holding down the "feed" button to give them multiple crops in one go!
[*] Mass alchemy ENABLED! The Alchemy Station now accepts up to 100 crops, bottles, and ash, and can produce 100 concoctions!
[*] Wearing your dancing shoes on the dancefloor in Ossono's Tavern now has a neat surprise 💃🕺
[*] If you're the kind of person that gets really attached to inanimate objects, then the new Item Frame is for you! Show off your favourite thing in your home!
[*] Concoctions can now be found in dungeon chests, hopefully making that one quest from your mother a little bit easier
[*] We made a lot of improvements to the targeting of placeable objects with both gamepad AND mouse! That's equality, baby!
[*] Gotta go fast, right? Now you can do more while sprinting: interact with objects and NPCs, place stuff, plant seeds, use items, eat crops, and MORE
[*] We also disabled the white outline on objects when the player is sprinting, so you won't be distracted from your go fast time
[*] Placing fences and bridges is now a bit faster, too! We removed the animation. It probably saves like 0.3 seconds, but it adds up, right?
[*] And the Spirit Brush is faster, too! We didn't remove the animation for it, because you gotta pet the lil guys, but we did speed it up. Zooooom
[/list]
Wow, what a lot of changes! Now we've just got the bug fixes to go...

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Adjusted Spirit pathfinding to stop wild spirits spawning in fenced areas on Rift island 
[*] Fixed an issue where player would get stuck in the mountain cave after opening Medallion
[*] The black rectangles that would sometimes pop up in your journal are GONE
[*] Fixed Spirits displaying behind dungeon doors
[*] Made sure that Ossono is actually attached to the balloon that floats away during her wedding
[*] Fixed an issue where you could propose to someone, cancel the proposal, leave the conversation, and start the conversation again, resulting in the dialogue skipping to the chat options. I mean, no offence, pals, but that's a really weird way to propose
[*] Fixed the Greenhouse Fishing loot becoming inaccessible 
[*] Fixed npcSpeechBubble 9-patch object
[*] Fixed a bug when some placeable objects didn’t stack after being picked up
[*] Fixed a few localization issues - title menu truncated in other languages, game files using incorrect font etc.
[/list]
THAT'S IT! Those are all the patch notes! My hand hurts from typing and my brain hurts from thinking. This is a four-page document. We've never had so many patch notes before. I need to lie down.

ENJOY MAGIC MAY!
Kate, Community Manager and owwy owwy wrist pain

notes.title: New FREE Magic Man Content Update and DLC is now LIVE!
notes.content:
Happy Magic May, everyone! Today, we're launching our latest update alongside some new DLC, both of which are themed around the mysterious man we all love to love: Waldo!

However! Our enigmatic wizard and chicken house aficionado may be the focus of this update, but that doesn't mean that's all you get. We've also added a bunch of new tweaks, content, and changes that will make the game even better than before.

[previewyoutube=penq0kbCHLc;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Magic May Update[/h1]

[b]Waldo (AKA Magic Man) finally figured out how to open his front door,[/b] and (if you've unlocked him moving to Moonstone Island) will now walk around town instead of hiding in his chicken house. 
He has new dialogue to acknowledge being back in town, and various other events!
The other Moonstone Islanders will also have new dialogue concerning Waldo and him being back in town, so it feels less... weird that he turned up after being missing for years and everyone's just totally fine with it.

[b]Waldo will also sell dozens of new cards in his shop![/b]
There will now be a party to celebrate you closing the rift, because that's kind of a big deal
Magic-themed furniture will be available for everyone, so you can add broom racks, scroll boxes, stained glass windows, and various witchy items to your house to make our Waldo feel right at home.

Now for the stuff that isn't Waldo-related:
[list]
[*] Fishbo! We're showing off our love for Moonstone Island's official unofficial mascot with a Fishbo-themed rug, a statue, and a fishbowl house. Now you can become as Fishbo.
[*] Extra, extra! Moonstone Island inhabitants discover napping! You can now sleep for short periods of time to regain energy, even if it's not bedtime!
[*] Map zooming! Revolutionary!!!
[*] Tired of living in a studio apartment? Why not try: WALLS! We've added placeable walls to the furniture catalog, so now you can divide up those rooms into much smaller rooms like the world's greediest landlord!
[*] Do you love to min-max? Are you an efficiency demon? Why not try the new, definitely unsafe, Perpetual FurnaceTM! It's a furnace that runs continuously and can be added to while running. Don't worry about emissions! The world is already in ruins!
[*] We've also invented the Perpetual Alchemy LabTM! You can now brew multiple concoctions at the same time, and add ingredients while it's running. Science!
[*] Four new Spirits, including one you might recognize from another Raw Fury game 👀
[*] Zed will now allow you to access the Spirit Storage at the Science Center even if he's not there. I guess you got a spare key or something? Use it wisely.
[*]New fishing lures that allow you to catch certain fish, because I *know* y'all have been struggling with finding that one particular fish like a really low-stakes Moby Dick
[*] A second tool wheel! Now you don't have to choose favorites! You can have ALL your tools ready to go!
[*] Do you really, really love a particular item? Attached to the stonefruit, perhaps? Or dreaming of showing off your favorite rock? Well, now you can, with the all-new ITEM FRAME!
[*] You can now press and hold to craft items and feed crops
[*] And the best thing of all: YOUR POCKETS JUST GOT BIGGER. We've added ten more inventory slots to EVERYONE'S game. For free. YEAHHHHH
[/list]

[h1]Arcane Artifacts DLC[/h1]

We're also launching our latest DLC! As always, this DLC is cosmetic only, and will not be required to unlock any extra content beyond the decor items that it comes with.

And here's what those decor items are:
[list]

[*] Magic Hat Rug
[*] Lectern

[*] Tattered Curtain
[/list]

As I always say, though – we've got more to come, folks. After all, we come out on Switch soon 😉 Also, it looks like we can all speak Russian now... weird how things just pop up like that!

notes.title: Slay the Spire Bundle!
notes.content:
Oh *hello* there, Alchemists!

 It's been a little while! Have you missed us? We've missed you. But we have returned, and we bring some *very* exciting news. As usual, I know. What can I say? We have a lot of exciting news here at the exciting news factory. That's what I like to call my office.

[h1]Exciting News #1
[/h1]
AAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!!!

Okay, sorry, it's just... this is very exciting for us. And me, personally. Okay. So.

WE'RE DOING A BUNDLE WITH SLAY THE SPIRE STARTING ON MARCH 14th!!!!!!!!

(What? WHAT?!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/a60f3fd8ca117e94632526de06d3988464f71888.jpg[/img]

YEAH!

(No, seriously, what? What's a bundle in this context?)

So, Moonstone Island and Slay The Spire have teamed up to create a card-loving, deck-building, lil-guy-fighting bundle, which means that you can buy Moonstone Island AND Slay The Spire as a bundle to get 10% off both! It was really hard to pick which one to add... because, like, who wants to befriend a teeny version of Gremlin Nob? Not me, that's for sure. I'm on Ascension 11! I just... sometimes make mistakes, y'know? And I have a personal grudge against Gremlin Nob. SUE ME.

We haven't confirmed an exact date yet (still workin' on it), but some time between March 20 and June 20, you'll get to see Moonstone Island on the Nintendo Switch. VERY COOL.

------

That's all the exciting news I can tell you right now, but it's NOT the only exciting news I've got cooking up. There are more cool things around the corner!

notes.title: The Village Post, Nov 2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/62c2c21417f1bfcce34aca835a23b79e55a22604.png[/img]

Happy November, everyone! As I write this, it's snowing hard outside. I live in Canada so everyone expects a lot of snow, but winter doesn't normally start until late December here, so this is unusual! It's very soft and quiet, though, so I'm not complaining. Also, I am sitting next to a fireplace so I'm quite cosy. Tell us your favorite season in the comments!

Before we get to the comments, though, let's dive back into what we've been up to.

[b]DLC/ EVENT RETROSPECTIVE
[/b]
This week we had TWO events: Holoween and Haikuween!

Holoween gave everyone who played the game between 30th October and 1st November three Holo-Hunter Potions, which increased the Holo Spirit encounter chances from 0.2% to 10%.

Haikuween asked people on our Discord, Twitter, and in these Steam posts to submit a spooky haiku or short poem to be in with a chance of winning a code for our Halloween DLC!

Both events are over now, but they were both a lot of fun. If you participated in either, thank you! We hope you now have many Holo Spirits and/or an appreciation for the art of haiku. We'll be announcing the winners on our Twitter, so keep an eye out!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/f81e452ab9694e1347cc998a292fe40fba901270.png[/img]

Just before Halloween, we released our biggest-ever update, which included a ton of new content, new Spirits, and a lot of bug fixes and much-requested updates to the game itself. 

The full patch notes are loooooooooooong, so here are the highlights:

[list]
[*] You can buy more rocks, grass, and trees to replace all the ones you destroyed
[*] NPCs will now accept gifts on their birthday even if you've given them two gifts that week
[*] Zed's Spirit Taming quest is easier to complete
[*] Boss Chests will keep their appearance after you steal them
[*] You can close mines, at last
[*] An even bigger greenhouse
[*] New furniture in Paolo's shop
[*] One-click stack transfer in the inventory 
[*] Adjustable day length
[*] A potion to reset your skills
[*] Plus: Various accessibility changes, card tweaks, and bug fixes
[/list]

[b]Here's the new free content:
[/b]
[list]
[*] Three new Spirits: Bonfire (Fire), Catsket (Dark), and Womr (Earth)
[*] A new Haunted House exterior
[*] Iron Bat Archway
[*] Gravestone
[*] Two skeletons
[*] Tiny skull
[*] Tongue rug

[*] We solved deforestation, you guys. Ofelia and Gaiana will now sell replantable trees
[*] We solved... de...rock...estation? Yeah, they also sell rocks

[*] You can now give an NPC a gift on their birthday, even if you've given them two gifts that week, because everyone likes birthday presents. Relatedly, it's my birthday tomorrow

[*] (One) Peace of mind: Treasure maps now clear properly, and are marked as complete properly too
[*] Rowan no longer wants the impossible gift of "Balloon". You can't have that, Rowan! You don't have the permits and you would almost definitely die
[*] Oh, you thought the greenhouse was already big enough? TOUGH LUCK, IT'S GONNA GET EVEN BIGGER. Gaiana and Ofelia will now let you buy an inadvisably large greenhouse for all your plant-growing desires
[*] Also, Paolo apparently wasn't selling, like, most of the furniture we made. Rude. We had a word, and now Paolo will sell LOADS of new furniture in their shop

[*] If your achievements weren't working, that should be fixed now too!

[*] Did you make a bad choice? It's okay, we've all been there. You can't change mistakes in real life, but you can change them in Moonstone Island with our new handy-dandy Skill Reset Potion! (disclaimer: do not try Skill Reset Potion in real life)

NEW

SPIRITS

notes.title: Let's Talk Temples!

Wait... no. Wrong temples. Today we're talking about Temples-with-a-capital-T, in the game Moonstone Island! These structures are NOT on the side of your face – they're hidden throughout the 100+ floating islands that surround Moonstone Island itself, and they're extremely important.

While adventuring, you may come across plenty of dungeons, each of which has treasures, traps, secrets, monsters, and a final boss, and Temples are very similar. But unlike dungeons, which are made up of lots of different pre-made rooms chosen at random, Temples are custom-built and unique. There are four of them in the world – one for each season – and each one contains a Magic Seal.

I won't tell you what those seals do... but they're very important.

Our Temples are all gigantic and very beautiful, but they're also a little hard to find. The Spring Temple will probably be your first one because it's veeeery close to the starting island...so you'll probably get to meet the Big Boss of the Spring Temple first. Again, I'm not tellin' ya nothin', but I'll give you a hint: Prepare for Earth-types!

Our Temples are really exciting, cool, gorgeous, and maybe even challenging! Challenging enough to start rubbing your face temples? Maybe...

notes.title: Introducing New Spirits: Dropple, Snaplant, and Bulbot!
notes.content:
Hello, Alchemists!

Do you like monster taming? 

Of course, you do. There's a reason why Pokémon is so successful, and it's basically because it's frowned upon to try to capture real-life animals and make them fight. Also, you're here, reading news about Moonstone Island, a game that prominently features monster taming!

So, we're on the Monster Tamer Direct, which is a neat little showcase of all things monstery-tamey, and as part of the fun, we showed off a few of our monsters (we call them Spirits, of course). Let's show them off a little bit more!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/661bdd91a1dd9d348cb6dbfc012a506650e8220d.jpg[/img]

Dropple is a Water-type Spirit, and while its name isn't exactly the finest of our Spirit-name puns (it's, uh, shaped like a drop, you see), that doesn't mean we don't love the lil guy. Dropple is cute, enthusiastic, and determined, with the unique ability "Salt Vs Steel", which reduces enemy Armor by one each round.

Now, we had to explain what salt vs steel meant for our localization team the other day, and we had a long, hard think about it. It turns out that steel, one of the beefiest, strongest substances around, is actually quite susceptible to corrosion and rust when it meets seawater – because of the salt. The phrase "salt vs steel" is supposed to mean that even the toughest things out there can be worn down with patience and resolve (and salt), which is what our diminutive friend Dropple is all about. 

Dropple may look tiny and weak, but don't count it out!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/da37fd3baaba7993402a7be458ddcc3f68511ea0.jpg[/img]

There are two Electric-type robot Spirits in Moonstone Island, and I like to think that they're family, or at the very least, they live on the same evolutionary branch. Armbot and Bulbot have a lot in common: they're both yellow, they have eyes, and they're made of metal and electricity. But today, we're talking about Bulbot. 

Bulbot looks like a lightbulb with arms, hence the name, and a big cyclopean eye right in the middle. Its special ability, if you'll forgive us for the awesome wordplay, is "Totally Lit", which illuminates dark rooms in dungeons. 

Let me explain how good this pun is. Something that is "totally lit" is very cool, you know? Like, "wow, that fluffy cow-print bucket hat is totally lit, bro!" But a room that is totally lit is just... literally totally lit. It has been lit up. Totally. Fully. 

I JUST THINK IT'S A REALLY GOOD PUN, OKAY?!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/21cdf7ade6b32abe60180983c1b1a29a23c54de5.jpg[/img]

Snaplant is one of our newer Spirits. Yeah, we're adding new Spirits, even this close to launch! Do you want to know how I know that Snaplant is new? Because I do not have its picture in my little list of Spirit pictures. I have to ask the lead developer to send me a new picture. This is a good thing, because now I can tell you how many Spirits we have in total, and it will be a bigger number than before. Hold on while I wait for the new Spirit pictures.

Okay gottem. 

Snaplant is a minion. Not like the yellow banana-loving guys, but a genuine minion. It's a little offshoot of [REDACTED], which is a [REDACTED] from the [REDACTED], which is very exciting! It'll provide support and cover for the [REDACTED], and generally run interference and make your life hard. Its ability, Potent Poison, will apply one Poison to your entire team every turn, so it's best to take out this Spirit ASAP (As Soon As Poison)!

notes.title: Welcome to new Alchemists!
notes.content:
Hello, Alchemists-to-be! 

We've seen a lot of new faces hit our Steam page since we announced our launch date last week, so, here's a big question: What exactly *is* Moonstone Island? I mean, what does it do? Where did it come from? And how does it work? 

We've been spending a lot of time talking about the nitty and the gritty of this game, but not the big picture. So, let's re-introduce you to the game!

Here's the elevator pitch. Come on, get in the elevator. What floor? 18? Okay, great. So, Moonstone Island is a creature-collecting, deckbuilding, farming-and-crafting life sim. What does that mean? It means that it's a big mashup of a lot of our favorite genres and mechanics! 

You play as an Alchemist-in-Training, who crashlands on a new island inhabited by a bunch of people who just so happen to be in need of an Alchemist. Your job is to tame and collect the errant Spirits that live on the outer islands and figure out a way to close the dangerous Rift that has formed in the sky. 

You'll be fighting other Spirits in tense card battles, and each one of your tamed Spirits will have their own deck that can change massively depending on your strategy, your luck, and the Spirit's elemental type. You'll also be able to level up Spirits through battles, making them stronger, faster, and probably wiser, too, and you can change and swap out their decks by removing, upgrading, and buying new cards.

But when you're not fighting Spirits, you're also taking care of yourself, the land, and your friendships. 

You can build and upgrade a house, going from a simple one-room tent to a sprawling four-floor mansion, complete with a kitchen, living room, craft room, potion room, furnace room, and whatever else your heart desires. You'll be able to craft your own furniture and even create custom wall and floor designs, so your house can look as unique as you want!

Outside the house is your garden, which can range from a simple little patio with cute furniture to a gigantic self-sustaining farm! There are about 50 different crops to grow, including some that can only be found in certain biomes, and many that only grow in a particular season. You can then use these crops to feed your Alchemist or Spirits to gain an edge in battle or out in the field, or you can combine them to create concoctions and potions with useful effects!

And what about those friendships, eh? We have 11 different NPCs that can all be befriended and even dated if you choose! Each character is unique and our cast is diverse – perhaps you'll end up hitting it off with nervous non-binary shopkeeper Rowan, or maybe you'll find a connection with the fierce but friendly Filipino botanist, Ofelia. Each one of these NPCs has their own story to tell through dates, as well as their own specially-tweaked rate of romance – some of them, like Gaiana, take longer to warm up to you – and you can even try dating them all if you want! 

Oh, sorry, did we miss your floor? Hold on, I'll press the button again and we can go back down. I promise I'm almost done.

There is so much more to discover beyond everything I've just said, including buried treasure, rare islands that only appear in specific circumstances, secrets hidden in ancient temples, and dungeons full of traps and monsters. We've really poured our whole hearts into this game, and we hope that you love it as much as we do.

Okay, that's it! That's Moonstone Island! We'll let you go now, but thank you so much for reading all of this. See you very soon!

~ Kate, Community Manager, and Elevator Enthusiast

notes.title: Let's Talk Story!
notes.content:
Good day, Alchemists!

Sure, you've left your house for training but there are lots of questions to be answered about your role in Moonstone Island. What are you doing on this island? Who are you? Why is there a weird man living in a chicken house?

Without spoiling too much, let's talk about STORY! 

A long time ago, the Cataclysm happened. We don't know much about what caused it, or why it happened, but we do know that it was something to do with the Spirits, and the Old Kingdom that existed on the surface of the planet. The Cataclysm caused huge chunks of earth to be flung into the troposphere, where they stay even now!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/0112c73bfa3d87ed9be5691c82cfa2c7117fd74a.jpg[/img]

In more recent history, Rifts started to open across the islands, allowing Dark Spirits to enter our world and cause havoc. The energy that escaped from the Rifts also angered the usually-peaceful Spirits, and so the Alchemist's Guild was formed to protect the islands from whatever was happening.

Each Alchemist is required to train for a year before becoming a full-fledged member of the Guild, and that's where we find you, dear player: an Alchemist about to begin their year-long training, and figuring out how to help and heal the world.

There's more story to discover, and we haven't really gone into the weird man in the chicken house at all, have we? But all your questions can, and will, be answered when the game comes out this Summer :D

~ Kate, Community Manager, and Wordsmith

notes.title: Let's Talk Cards!
notes.content:
Hey, Alchemists!

We're coming up to the end of the Next Fest demo, but don't worry – Moonstone Island will be out this Summer, so you won't have long to wait for the full game (and we won't boot you out after two weeks, either!)

Today, we wanted to show off some of the cards in our game. We're really influenced by games like Slay the Spire, where individual cards can make or break a deck, but you can also create decks that center around one particular mechanic.

Turns out deckbuilding is really hard! You have to focus on balance and creating mechanics and systems that tie into each other in a really satisfying way. We like it a lot, though, and we're really proud of the cards we've created. We know that not all cozy gamers are versed at card-games, so let's break down our cards:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/f20ba7576f368519bdb27c571193d83c905dd5eb.jpg[/img]

[b]Title: [/b]The name of the card! If it has a little + next to it, it's the upgraded version.
[b]Type:[/b] Skill or Attack. Pretty self-explanatory!
[b]Element: [/b]This matches the type of the Spirit it belongs to. If the enemy Spirits are weak to it, it does extra damage and removes their Armor!
[b]Cost:[/b] How many of your Energy points the card costs. Some are free, others cost all your Energy!
[b]Rarity: [/b]This rating tells you how rare and also how powerful a card is. The rarity scale goes up to 9!
[b]Description:[/b] Tells you what the card does.

So, this card is called Calm Spirit, and it's not very rare at all. It costs 1 Energy, as you can see in the top-left corner, and it has three effects: it draws one card, removes one Armor, and inflicts Calm on the Spirit, which stops it from playing Attack cards for one turn.

Here, you can see three Tackle cards, each doing different damage based on the Spirit's Attack stat, and whether or not the card is upgraded. Tackle cards are the basic cards that all Spirits have, along with Bash cards, which reduce Armor. You can get rid of these cards if you want, but we hear there are cards out there that work well with a Tackle-filled deck...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/7260fbbea4b0d65701dbead4c08faf55dff72e98.jpg[/img]

Here's a slightly rarer card – it's Burgloon's 'Flip Switch', which costs 2 Energy, and deals 8 Electric damage, three times. Combine this with the Attack-boosting Charge buff, and take the Armor off the enemy, and you could be doing massive amounts of damage, because Charge increases the damage of each attack. Instead of hitting for 8 damage, you could be hitting for 15 damage... three times.

We can't wait to hear what kind of decks and strategies you've figured out! The exciting part of making a deck builder is that the power is in the player's hands – there are combos out there that we don't even know about!

~ Kate, community Manager, and Card Shark

notes.title: Let's Talk Crafting!
notes.content:
Hello, Alchemists!

Our topic of the day today is:

[b]🛠 Crafting! 🛠 [/b]

We have a lot of crafting systems on Moonstone Island. If you're the type of person who loves baking your own bread and sewing your own clothes, you're going to have a great time. And if you're not? You'll have a great time too! Everybody wins!!!

[b]Alchemy Table[/b]
Make concoctions! You are an Alchemist, after all. At your Alchemy Table, you can combine ingredients to brew up special elixirs that combine the effects of two crops for extra-efficient Stamina restoration, Spirit taming, and more! 

Just make sure you have enough ash to power the alchemy. We won't tell you how you get ash, but let's just say that you need to set wood on fire somehow...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/25bb5fafaa6413eb016b373458ce69ba4860bb50.jpg[/img]

[b]Cauldron[/b]
The Cauldron lets you live out your witchy fantasies as you brew potions that can help you see in the dark, run faster, and even slow down time. Experiment to find new combinations!

[b]Decoration Station[/b]
Give our carpenter Paolo a run for his money by making your very own furniture! Chairs, sofas, bookshelves, and even cute little kitchens are within reach, as long as you have the materials to make 'em.

[b]Loom[/b]
Do your walls look boring? Design your own wallpaper and flooring with the Loom! You can draw out cute pixel designs and then plaster them all over your house to make it suuuuper cute and totally custom.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/a50695c92b13b92733e79a32bb18e8c5049b55e9.jpg[/img]

[b]Moonstone Enchanter[/b]
Some things need just a little more magic, and that's where the Moonstone Enchanted comes in. Anything you need that requires arcane power can be found on this crafting table, whether it's a barn for your Spirits, a house that's secretly a pocket dimension, or a glider that can get you around the skies much faster than your broom. 

You'll need a lot of Moonstones for these crafting recipes, so seek them out at night!

[b]Furnace & Anvil[/b]
Ferra won't let you borrow her blacksmithery (it's too expensive to run!) so you'll have to build your own. Smelt down metal ore in the furnace, and then hammer it into special protective charms that can shield you from electric, poison, and dark damage when you're out exploring on the more dangerous islands!

~ Kate, Community Manager, and Crafting Curator

notes.title: Let's Talk Spirits!
notes.content:
Good day to you all, Alchemists! 

Today, we're showing off another feature of the game:

🔮 Spirits! 🔮

You may have heard Moonstone Island referred to as a "Pokémon-meets-Stardew game", and it's the creature-collecting aspect that we're talking about today. Our creatures are called Spirits, and they form the backbone of Moonstone Island's card-combat system. There's a lot to say about Spirits, so let's get stuck in!

Each one of our Spirits is a completely unique design, and our ideas for the Spirits can come from just about anywhere. Some of them are simple combinations, like a beach ball with sunglasses, while others are inspired by our favorite things, like Ghibli movies (seriously, we've got a lot of Ghibli references).

They're all matched up to an elemental type, too, and we have eight elements in total: Earth, Water, Poison, Electric, Fire, Dark, Psychic, and Ice. They also have weaknesses, one that is based on their type (so, Fire is weak to Water) and one that is randomly chosen, just to keep things a little unpredictable!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/2ab727d2834fc82cec4ea6990973554a59a9bebe.png[/img]

Every single Spirit also has its own ability, some of which affect the battle, but some of which affect other things, like your walk speed, your likelihood of finding treasure, or your success rate with flirting. It's quite fun to figure out which Spirits do what to really get the ball rolling! You can have up to three Spirits in your Medallion – the team that's out in the field with you – and you can have up to three Spirits follow you around, too.

Finally, every Spirit will drop special elemental Spirit resources. We hear that someone in town might be researching these resources, and might even pay you for filling up your Spirit encyclopedia. But that's all we know...

Our aim is 100 spirits for the launch, so follow us along on our journey as we unveil new little guys for you to collect!

~ Kate, Community Manager, and Spirit Wrangler

notes.title: Let's Talk Adventuring!
notes.content:
Welcome back, Alchemists! 

We're going to be highlighting an important aspect of the game for you!

Today, it's all about...

🧹 Adventuring! 🧹

With over 100 procedurally-generated islands to explore, there is LOTS to discover on the Moonstone Island archipelago. Each island has a unique shape – some are even cheeky references if you can spot them – and there are multiple biomes to discover, too. 

You can find the perilous, static islands of the Electric biome, or the noxious gases of the Poison biome, or make your home-away-from-home on the beachy Water Biome. You can even craft protective charms to make the dangers of the Fire biome and the scary Dark biome a breeze!

You'll need some gear before you step out of your comfort zone, though. You'll start the game with a broom, and then get downgraded to a balloon because of your bad flying... but you can build yourself a new broom if you find the balloon too tedious! Eventually, you may even want to upgrade to something a bit fancier.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/ec9bf945d26474dd50e9b24847941e58258db629.jpg[/img]

You'll also need provisions! Crops can restore your Stamina, heal your Spirits, and tame your opponents, too, so you can build up a team that's suited to the particular biome you're in. After all, every Spirit has its elemental strengths and weaknesses, so do your research to give yourself a fighting chance!

And while you're at it, why not pick up some new crops and materials? Every island and biome has its unique crops, which you can take back to the main island to propagate and get more seeds. You can find wood and stone pretty much anywhere, but the fish you'll find in the rivers and ponds are indigenous to specific biomes, just like the crops, so make sure to fish whenever and wherever you can!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40678838/c851a11fac6c16ac3447ca0ef96ec9a5c8868b60.jpg[/img]

We also hear rumors that some islands have dungeons, mines, and hidden treasure chests that can provide you with super-rare and super-helpful new items and plants... But we'll say no more about that!

Until next time, brew on!

~ Kate, Community Manager, and Treasure Hunter
